subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should OpenClaw permanently treat ClawHub, bundled metadata, official-catalog mappings, and tracked updates as acknowledgement-free while requiring `--force` or an interactive prompt for new arbitrary executable sources?
rationale: Tests prove the implementation, but cannot determine which source classes deserve implicit trust or whether broadening the public `--force` contract is the intended long-term security and upgrade policy.

options.title: Approve the proposed trust matrix
options.body: Accept the centralized exemptions and dual-purpose `--force` behavior with the current proof and compatibility notes.

options.title: Separate acknowledgement semantics
options.body: Keep overwrite behavior isolated and introduce a distinct maintainer-approved source-confirmation mechanism.

options.title: Narrow trusted sources
options.body: Require acknowledgement for one or more currently exempt source classes and update the proof and documentation.

recommendation.title: Approve the proposed trust matrix
recommendation.body: Accept the centralized exemptions and dual-purpose `--force` behavior with the current proof and compatibility notes.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history most strongly connects this person to the plugin installation, catalog, and persistence surfaces affected by the policy.
